title: Vehicle Speed Sensor "A"
plain: The engine computer isn't getting a usable signal from the sensor that tells it how fast the car is moving.
symptoms: Speedometer not working or jumping around
ABS or traction control light may come on

causes.name: Damaged wiring or corroded connector at the sensor
Faulty ABS wheel speed sensor (on cars that use it for road speed)
Damaged sensor drive gear or tone ring

checks: Note whether the speedometer works
Inspect the speed sensor wiring and connector for damage or oil
Check for ABS wheel speed sensor codes, which may be the real source
Watch the speed reading on a scan tool while driving
fix: Usually a new vehicle speed sensor or a wiring repair at the sensor connector.
drive: Drive with care and get it checked soon. The speedometer may be wrong, shifting can be harsh or erratic, and ABS or traction control may not work. Judge your speed by the flow of traffic, stay in the right lane and leave extra following distance. Take it easy on slick roads.
test_first: Compare vehicle speed and wheel speed readings on a scan tool, inspect the sensor wiring and connector, and check the drive gear or tone ring before replacing the sensor.

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor "A" Range/Performance
plain: The vehicle speed sensor is sending a reading that doesn't make sense or doesn't match other sensors. This part tells the computer how fast the car is moving.

causes.name: Faulty or sluggish vehicle speed sensor
Wrong tire size or axle ratio not matching the computer setting
Wiring or connector problem skewing the reading

checks: Compare the vehicle speed sensor reading on a scan tool with real conditions
Confirm the tire size and gear ratio match the original setup
Inspect the wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
fix: Usually a new vehicle speed sensor or repair of the underlying problem, after ruling out wiring.

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor "A" Circuit Low Input
plain: The signal from the vehicle speed sensor is lower than it should ever be, which usually points to a wiring short or a failed sensor. This part tells the computer how fast the car is moving.

causes.name: Problem with the sensor's reference voltage supply

checks: Inspect the wiring and connector for rubbing, damage or corrosion
Check reference voltage and ground at the connector with a meter
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new vehicle speed sensor if it tests bad.

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor "A" Intermittent/Erratic/High
plain: The signal from the vehicle speed sensor keeps cutting in and out or jumping around. This part tells the computer how fast the car is moving.

causes.name: Chafed wiring that shorts or opens over bumps

checks: Wiggle the harness and connector while watching live data on a scan tool
Look for chafed wires near hot or moving parts
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new vehicle speed sensor if it tests bad.

title: Brake Switch "A"/"B" Correlation
plain: The brake pedal switch sends two signals that should always agree, and the computer saw them disagree.
symptoms: Brake lights may stay on or not work
Push-button start or shifting out of Park may not work normally

causes.name: Misadjusted brake light switch or broken pedal stopper pad
Wiring or connector problem at the switch

checks: Have someone confirm the brake lights come on and go off with the pedal
Look for a missing or broken plastic stopper pad on the brake pedal arm
Check the stop lamp fuse
Compare both switch signals on a scan tool while pressing the pedal
fix: Most often a new brake light switch, adjusted correctly.
examples: Often seen on Hyundai and Kia models with a failing brake light switch
drive: This code doesn't normally reduce braking power, but your brake lights may not work or may stay on, which raises the risk of being rear-ended. Have someone check your brake lights; if they're out, avoid driving until it's fixed. Cruise control and shifting out of Park may also act up.
test_first: Check the brake light switch adjustment and pedal stopper pad, the stop lamp fuse, and compare both switch signals on a scan tool before replacing the switch.

title: Idle Control System
plain: The computer can't control the engine's idle speed the way it expects to.
symptoms: Idle speed too high or too low
Engine stalls when coming to a stop

causes.name: Dirty throttle body or idle air control valve
Wiring problem to the idle control valve or electronic throttle
Idle relearn needed after cleaning or a battery disconnect

checks: Clean the throttle body and idle air passages
Check for vacuum leaks around hoses and the intake
Test the idle air control valve and its wiring
Perform an idle relearn if the vehicle needs one
fix: Often a throttle body and idle air control valve cleaning; replace the valve if it tests bad.
examples: Well known on 1990s and 2000s Honda models with a dirty or failing idle air control valve
drive: If the engine stalls when you stop, limit driving and get it checked soon; a stall can leave you with heavy steering and brakes in traffic. If the idle is just a bit off, you can usually drive to a shop. A high idle can push the car forward at stops, so keep firm brake pressure.
test_first: Clean and inspect the throttle body or idle air valve, check for vacuum leaks and wiring faults, and do an idle relearn before replacing the idle valve or throttle body.

title: Idle Control System RPM Lower Than Expected
plain: The engine is idling slower than the computer is asking for, even after it tried to raise the idle.
symptoms: Shaking at idle, often worse with the A/C on

causes.name: Dirty throttle body with carbon buildup
Faulty idle air control valve or electronic throttle body
Clogged air filter or restricted intake
Extra engine load from a dragging accessory

checks: Clean the throttle body and check that the throttle plate moves freely
Check the air filter and intake for restrictions
Watch commanded vs actual idle speed on a scan tool
fix: Most often a throttle body cleaning and idle relearn; a new idle valve or throttle body if cleaning does not help.

cost.job: Clean throttle body and idle passages

drive: If it stalls at stops, limit driving and get it checked soon, since a stall in traffic makes steering and braking much harder. If the idle is just low or shaky, you can usually drive gently to a shop.
test_first: Clean the throttle body, check the air filter, PCV valve and accessory drive for drag, and do an idle relearn before replacing the idle valve or throttle body.

title: Idle Control System RPM Higher Than Expected
plain: The engine is idling faster than the computer wants, even after it tried to bring the idle down.
symptoms: Car pushes forward harder at stops
Revs slow to drop after letting off the gas

causes.name: Vacuum leak from a cracked hose or intake gasket
Dirty or sticking throttle body or idle air control valve
Faulty idle air control valve or electronic throttle body
Idle relearn needed after battery disconnect or cleaning

checks: Listen and smoke-test for vacuum leaks
Clean the throttle body and idle air passages
Check the PCV valve and hoses
Perform an idle relearn
fix: Usually fixing a vacuum leak or cleaning the throttle body, then an idle relearn.

cost.job: Repair vacuum leak and clean throttle body

drive: It usually doesn't change how the car drives, so book a repair, but the car may push forward harder at stops, so keep firm pressure on the brake. If the revs hang high, surge on their own or the car is hard to hold at a stop, get it checked right away.
test_first: Smoke test for vacuum leaks, check the PCV valve and hoses, clean and inspect the throttle body or idle valve, and do an idle relearn before replacing parts.

title: Idle Air Control System Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees lower voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the idle air control valve, often from a wire shorted to ground. This part controls how much air bypasses the throttle to set idle speed.
symptoms: Idle too high, too low or unstable
checks: Inspect the idle air control valve wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the idle air control valve with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new idle air control valve if it tests bad.

title: Idle Air Control System Circuit High
plain: The computer sees higher voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the idle air control valve, often from a wire shorted to power or a failed part. This part controls how much air bypasses the throttle to set idle speed.
symptoms: Idle too high, too low or unstable

causes.name: Faulty or shorted idle air control valve

checks: Inspect the idle air control valve wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the idle air control valve with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new idle air control valve if it tests bad.

title: Cold Start Idle Air Control System Performance
plain: On a cold start the computer raises idle speed to heat the catalytic converter quickly, and the idle did not reach its target.
symptoms: Idle may be lower or higher than normal right after a cold start

causes.name: Faulty electronic throttle body or idle air control valve
Engine computer software needing an update

checks: Clean the throttle body and check for vacuum leaks
Look for a manufacturer service bulletin or software update (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Usually a throttle body cleaning or vacuum leak repair; some models need a computer update.

title: Cold Start Ignition Timing Performance
plain: On a cold start the computer delays spark timing to warm the catalytic converter, and it could not hold the timing where it wanted.
symptoms: Possible rough idle right after a cold start

causes.name: Dirty throttle body or vacuum leak upsetting idle control
Engine computer software needing an update

checks: Check for other idle, misfire or knock codes and fix those first
Look for a manufacturer service bulletin or software update (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Fix any idle air or misfire problem first; some models need a computer update.

title: Cold Start Engine Coolant Temperature Performance
plain: During the cold start check, the engine coolant temperature did not behave the way the computer expected.
symptoms: Temperature gauge may read low or warm up slowly
Heater may be slow to get warm

causes.name: Wiring problem at the coolant temperature sensor

checks: Check the coolant level
Watch coolant temperature on a scan tool as the engine warms up
Check whether the thermostat opens too early
fix: Usually a new thermostat or coolant temperature sensor.

title: Cold Start Rough Idle
plain: The computer noticed the engine idling roughly during the first minutes after a cold start.
symptoms: Shaking or rough idle when the engine is cold

causes.name: Worn spark plugs or weak ignition coil
Carbon buildup on intake valves (direct injection engines)

checks: Check for misfire codes and misfire counts on a scan tool
Inspect spark plugs and coils
Check for vacuum leaks
fix: Usually ignition parts or a vacuum leak repair; carbon cleaning on some direct injection engines.

title: Cold Start Engine Exhaust Temperature Too Low
plain: After a cold start the exhaust did not heat up as fast as the computer expected, so the catalytic converter may be slow to start working.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Cold start idle or timing strategy not working (dirty throttle body or vacuum leak)
Engine computer software needing an update
Exhaust leak near the front of the exhaust

checks: Check for other cold start, idle or thermostat codes
Look for a manufacturer service bulletin or software update (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Repair any idle or thermostat problem; some vehicles need a computer software update.

title: Brake Assist Vacuum Too Low
plain: The computer sees too little vacuum in the brake booster, so the brakes may take more effort to stop the car.
symptoms: Hard brake pedal that needs more push
Hissing sound near the brake pedal or booster
Check engine or brake warning light on

causes.name: Cracked or disconnected brake booster vacuum hose
Weak engine vacuum pump (on engines that use one)

checks: Inspect the booster vacuum hose and check valve
Check booster vacuum with a gauge
Listen for hissing at the booster with the engine running
fix: Usually a vacuum hose or check valve; a new brake booster or vacuum pump if those test bad.

title: Closed Throttle Position Switch
plain: The switch that tells the computer the throttle is fully closed (foot off the gas) isn't reading correctly. Mostly found on older vehicles.
symptoms: Possible stalling when coming to a stop

causes.name: Faulty or misadjusted closed throttle switch or throttle position sensor
Sticking throttle linkage or dirty throttle body

checks: Check that the throttle closes fully and smoothly
Watch the closed throttle signal on a scan tool while opening and closing the throttle
fix: Usually a throttle position sensor or switch, or a throttle body cleaning.

title: Idle Air Control Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem, such as a broken connection, in the circuit it uses to control the idle air control valve. This part controls how much air bypasses the throttle to set idle speed.
symptoms: Idle too high, too low or unstable

causes.name: Broken wire or loose or corroded connector

checks: Inspect the idle air control valve wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the idle air control valve with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new idle air control valve if it tests bad.

title: Starter Request Circuit
plain: The signal that asks the computer to crank the engine, from the key or start button, is not behaving as expected.
symptoms: Engine may not crank, or cranks only sometimes

causes.name: Faulty ignition switch or start button
Faulty clutch or neutral safety switch
Wiring or connector problem in the start circuit

checks: Try starting in Neutral or with the clutch fully pressed
Check the start signal on a scan tool while turning the key or pressing the button
fix: Usually an ignition switch, start button, safety switch or wiring repair.

title: Incorrect Immobilizer Key
plain: The anti-theft system doesn't recognize the key, so the computer may block the engine from starting.
symptoms: Engine will not start, or starts and dies right away

causes.name: Key not programmed to the vehicle
Faulty antenna ring around the ignition

checks: Try the spare key
Replace the key fob battery on push-button start cars
Have a shop or dealer check key programming
fix: Usually programming or replacing the key; sometimes an antenna or immobilizer module.

title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The battery temperature sensor is sending a reading that doesn't make sense or doesn't match other sensors. This part helps the computer adjust charging voltage to the battery temperature.
symptoms: Battery may be undercharged or overcharged

causes.name: Faulty or sluggish battery temperature sensor
Sensor not seated against the battery after a battery replacement
Wiring or connector problem skewing the reading

checks: Compare the battery temperature sensor reading on a scan tool with real conditions
Make sure the sensor is clipped in place at the battery
Inspect the wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
fix: Usually a new battery temperature sensor or repair of the underlying problem, after ruling out wiring.

title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit
plain: The computer has spotted a problem in the wiring circuit for the battery temperature sensor. This part helps the computer adjust charging voltage to the battery temperature.
symptoms: Battery may be undercharged or overcharged

causes.name: Damaged wiring or a loose or corroded connector
Blown fuse or missing power or ground to the sensor

checks: Inspect the battery temperature sensor wiring and connector for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check related fuses and confirm power and ground at the sensor
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new battery temperature sensor if it tests bad.

title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
plain: The signal from the battery temperature sensor is lower than it should ever be, which usually points to a wiring short or a failed sensor. This part helps the computer adjust charging voltage to the battery temperature.
symptoms: Battery may be undercharged or overcharged

causes.name: Problem with the sensor's reference voltage supply

checks: Inspect the wiring and connector for rubbing, damage or corrosion
Check reference voltage and ground at the connector with a meter
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new battery temperature sensor if it tests bad.

title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit High
plain: The signal from the battery temperature sensor is higher than it should ever be, which usually points to a broken wire, bad ground or a failed sensor. This part helps the computer adjust charging voltage to the battery temperature.
symptoms: Battery may be undercharged or overcharged

causes.name: Broken wire or poor ground in the sensor circuit
Signal wire shorted to a voltage source

checks: Inspect the wiring and connector for broken wires or corrosion
Check reference voltage and ground at the connector with a meter
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new battery temperature sensor if it tests bad.

title: Idle Air Control Circuit Intermittent
plain: The circuit that controls the idle air control valve is cutting in and out.
symptoms: Idle speed that surges or drops at random

causes.name: Loose or corroded connector at the idle air control valve

checks: Wiggle the harness while watching idle speed
Inspect the connector pins for corrosion
fix: Usually a connector or wiring repair, or a new idle air control valve.

title: Idle Air Control System Performance
plain: The idle speed isn't responding properly when the computer adjusts the idle air control system.
symptoms: Stalling when coming to a stop

causes.name: Dirty throttle body or idle air passages
Faulty idle air control valve or electronic throttle body

checks: Clean the throttle body and idle passages
Check for vacuum leaks
Perform an idle relearn
fix: Usually a throttle body cleaning or vacuum leak repair, then an idle relearn.

title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor Circuit
plain: The computer has spotted a problem in the wiring circuit for the crankcase pressure sensor. This part monitors pressure inside the engine crankcase to check the PCV system.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Damaged wiring or a loose or corroded connector
Blown fuse or missing power or ground to the sensor

checks: Inspect the crankcase pressure sensor wiring and connector for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check related fuses and confirm power and ground at the sensor
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new crankcase pressure sensor if it tests bad.

title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The crankcase pressure sensor is sending a reading that doesn't make sense or doesn't match other sensors. This part monitors pressure inside the engine crankcase to check the PCV system.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Faulty or sluggish crankcase pressure sensor
Clogged, cracked or disconnected PCV hose or valve
Wiring or connector problem skewing the reading

checks: Compare the crankcase pressure sensor reading on a scan tool with real conditions
Inspect the PCV valve, oil separator and hoses
Inspect the wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
fix: Usually a new crankcase pressure sensor or repair of the underlying problem, after ruling out wiring.

title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
plain: The signal from the crankcase pressure sensor is lower than it should ever be, which usually points to a wiring short or a failed sensor. This part monitors pressure inside the engine crankcase to check the PCV system.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Problem with the sensor's reference voltage supply

checks: Inspect the wiring and connector for rubbing, damage or corrosion
Check reference voltage and ground at the connector with a meter
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new crankcase pressure sensor if it tests bad.

title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor Circuit High
plain: The signal from the crankcase pressure sensor is higher than it should ever be, which usually points to a broken wire, bad ground or a failed sensor. This part monitors pressure inside the engine crankcase to check the PCV system.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Broken wire or poor ground in the sensor circuit
Signal wire shorted to a voltage source

checks: Inspect the wiring and connector for broken wires or corrosion
Check reference voltage and ground at the connector with a meter
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new crankcase pressure sensor if it tests bad.

title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
plain: The signal from the crankcase pressure sensor keeps cutting in and out or jumping around. This part monitors pressure inside the engine crankcase to check the PCV system.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Chafed wiring that shorts or opens over bumps

checks: Wiggle the harness and connector while watching live data on a scan tool
Look for chafed wires near hot or moving parts
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new crankcase pressure sensor if it tests bad.

title: Positive Crankcase Ventilation Filter Restriction
plain: The filter or separator that lets oil vapor vent from inside the engine is clogged, so pressure can build up in the crankcase.
symptoms: Oil leaks from seals or gaskets

causes.name: Clogged PCV filter or oil separator
Excess blow-by from worn piston rings

checks: Inspect and replace the PCV filter or oil separator
Check the oil condition and change interval
fix: Usually a new PCV filter or oil separator.
